extracted.intended_audience: architects, builders, students of architecture, and educated travellers interested in Venetian Gothic/domestic architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative standards for applying Gothic forms and ornament to domestic/building design (windows, doors, porches, courts, decoration) with attention to structural honesty, symbolism, and local tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Gothic form for durability, dignity, and honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: “I plead for the introduction of the Gothic form into our domestic architecture, not merely because it is lovely, but because it is the only form of faithful, strong, enduring, and honorable building, in such materials as come daily to our hands.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gothic form is recommended because it gives security and dignity to work wrought with imperfect means and materials; contrasted with modern cheap work which requires scale/cost to last. Use Gothic where longevity, structural truth, and moral/esthetic honesty are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject false economy and dishonesty in construction
rubrics_metrics.description: “dishonesty and false economy will no more build safely in Gothic than in any other style” and bad building practices cause frequent catastrophes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cost-cutting, shoddy materials, contract/cheap work, stucco/plaster expedients and dishonest ironwork; such practices produce rotten timbers, baseless bridges, fungous walls, and high long-term social/national cost (repairs, condemnation, pulling down).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pointed arch (voussoir construction) for structural openings
rubrics_metrics.description: The pointed arch is structurally superior to the level lintel of the square window; it sustains the building above and endures in inferior materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer pointed/arched heads for windows and doors because they distribute loads reliably even in imperfect brick/stone. Examples: Veronese Gothic brick arches surviving since the 13th century; contrast with flat brick lintels which split and produce wide fissures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid square-headed windows with level brick lintels
rubrics_metrics.description: “the common square window is the worst; and its level head of brickwork ... is the weakest way of covering a space.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Square-headed openings with level brickwork are prone to failure even when carefully built (sometimes fail within years); common anti-patterns include supporting bricks temporarily on lath while mortar dries. Replace with pointed arches or true voussoir construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointed arches are compatible with modern glazing and sashes
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not the smallest necessity, because the arch is pointed, that the aperture should be so [i.e., inconvenient]; the work of the arch is to sustain the building above; when this is once done the pointed head of it may be filled in any way we choose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filling the arch head (e.g., with a stone shield, sculptured tympanum, grouped lancet windows) allows equal or better light and sash adjustment than square windows. Use lancet groups, filled tympana, and proper glazing details to combine Gothic form with modern convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer steeply vaulted, sheltered Gothic porches over Greek porticoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of the base and almost useless Greek portico, letting the rain and wind enter it at will, build the steeply vaulted and completely sheltered Gothic porch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design entrance porches to be fully sheltered and vaulted, protecting entry from weather and providing a decorated, functional threshold; embellish with gables, sculpture, and color rather than superficial classical porticos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide fields for rich decoration and encourage local workmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: On all these fields for rich decoration let the common workman carve what he pleases, to the best of his power, and we may have a school of domestic architecture ... which will make our children grateful to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tympana, gables, porches and other surfaces as opportunities for sculpture, color, and inlaid patterns. Allow and commission skilled local workmen to execute carving and ornament, fostering craft traditions and varied, expressive domestic ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrances should express family identity and trust in God
rubrics_metrics.description: In the earlier ages ... the name of the family is told, and together with it there is always an intimation that they have placed their defence and their prosperity in God's hands ... In the centre of the archivolt we find almost invariably ... the hand between the sun and moon in the attitude of blessing ... On the tympanum is the shield of the family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design doorways to bear the family's heraldry, protective religious symbols (angel, hand between sun and moon), or inscriptions of blessing where appropriate. When elaborate sculpture is impossible, simpler devices (suspended shield, cross) may be used. Avoid stripping all symbolic meaning in the name of decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use archivolt and tympanum sculpture to reflect cultural/seasonal programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The sculptures represent the months of the year employed in the avocations usually attributed to them ... The months are personified as follows: January ... February ... etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate locally meaningful iconography (months, zodiac signs, agricultural occupations) into archivolts and other sculptural programs to connect building ornament with climate, seasonality, and regional practice. Be attentive to regional variants between Italian and Northern motifs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design doorways to evolve from small square-headed entries to pointed arches with filled tympanum
rubrics_metrics.description: In private palaces the entrance ... is nearly always square-headed in the earliest examples, without any arch above, but afterwards the arch is thrown across above the lintel. The interval between the two, or tympanum, is filled with sculpture, or closed by iron bars, with sometimes a projecting gable, to form a porch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing or restoring doors, prefer the matured Gothic solution: a pointed arch thrown across above a lintel, a filled tympanum (sculpture or grating), and a projecting gabled porch. Avoid small, ill-proportioned square-headed entries without architectural shelter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize palaces around an interior court with external stair and central well
rubrics_metrics.description: The gateways ... almost universally lead, in the earlier palaces, into a long interior court, round which the mass of the palace is built; and in which its first story is reached by a superb external staircase, sustained on four or five pointed arches ... In the centre of the court there is always a marble well; and these wells furnish some of the most superb examples of Venetian sculpture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan domestic palaces with a central court, a prominent external staircase to the noble floor, carved parapets, projecting balconies, and a sculptural well at center. Treat wells and court elements as sculptural/familial display (shields, foliage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan interiors around a noble hall lit by principal window groups and decorated ceilings
rubrics_metrics.description: The interior apartments always consist of one noble hall on the first story ... extending across the entire depth of the house, and lighted in front by the principal groups of its windows, while smaller apartments open from it on either side. The ceilings ... are of bold horizontal beams, richly carved and gilded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a principal, large hall (often on the first or second story) across the building depth, lit by grouped principal windows; subordinate rooms should open from this hall. Use boldly carved and gilded beam ceilings where appropriate; decorative painting may replace original Gothic ceilings in later remodeling but the plan logic should remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ color in Gothic exterior decoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the color decorations of the Gothic exteriors I have, therefore, at present taken no notice, as it will be more convenient to embrace this subject in one general view ... when we arrive at the period of its richest development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include polychromy and color schemes as an integral part of Gothic exterior design; treat colored inlays, mosaic, and painted surfaces as part of the ornament program rather than mere afterthoughts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor meaningful religious/familial symbolism over meaningless classical ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaningless doorway is merely an ignorant copy of heathen models ... The Renaissance architects perceived the irrationality of all this, cut away both crosses and angels, and substituted heads of satyrs ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid adopting classical or Palladian ornament devoid of local or spiritual meaning. Prefer genuine religious or heraldic symbolism (crosses, angels, inscriptions) that communicates the owner's beliefs and identity, rather than empty classical motifs which may amount to an ignorant or hypocritical pastiche.
